records.reason: limitedUses carries only the frequency; the verdict's justification for adding nothing else — "the value moves on allies or on foes, not on your sheet" — is contradicted by the app's own data. Battle auras are exactly two spells (feats['aura-enhancement']: "Add Benediction and Malediction … These spells are also battle auras"), and spells['benediction'] reads "You AND YOUR ALLIES gain a +1 status bonus to AC while within the emanation." So raising a Benediction you have active raises YOUR OWN AC status bonus, +1 → +2 (max +4), for the rest of its duration. Nothing carries it: the feat has no field, is absent from situationalBonuses.ts, and there is no benediction mode (0 of the 225 core.modes reference it), so the increase lands on no surface at all. A star on AC is the app's existing shape for a triggered, duration-limited status bonus to your own AC (cf. "arc-of-destruction" +4 status AC vs the triggering Strike). Only the Benediction half is expressible — Malediction's penalty is target-side (ruling D) and is deliberately left out.
records.quote: Choose one active battle aura you have; that battle aura's status bonus or penalty increases by 1, to a maximum of 4. This value remains for the rest of the aura's duration.

The reason given for dropping the +1 — "SituationalTarget.kind has no counteract member … the printed skill is also missing from the record's text, so naming one would be inventing it" — sets a standard the same sweep abandons two rows earlier. The counteract check is not a stat of its own: the record itself says "you use either your ⟨⟩ or ⟨⟩ modifier as your counteract modifier", so the roll IS a skill check and a +1 circumstance bonus to it is a skill bonus. NaturalAttack.die is documented as a single die — types.ts:1670 "Damage die, e.g. 'd6' / 'd8'. Base count is one die (Handwraps striking adds more)" — and deriveUnarmedStrike hard-codes `const dice = 1 + strikingExtra` then formats `${dice}${die}` (derive.ts:1528, 1554). GrantedStrike/NaturalAttack has no dice-count field at all, so a 3-die base cannot be expressed: this needs a `dice` field on GrantedStrike + NaturalAttack (threaded into deriveUnarmedStrike's `dice`), not a data row. Etching CONSUMES the loose rune inventory entry — attachments.ts planRune returns `consume: true` for a property rune, and InventoryTab.tsx:897 runs `removeInventoryItem(next, srcId)` — and explain.ts:198 states it outright: "Etching CONSUMES the loose rune item and records its id here, so `inv.itemId` never names it." `passiveItemBonus` (derive.ts:205-226) only reads `db.items[inv.itemId]?.passiveEffects` (and c.resolvedItemPassives[inv.itemId]) for inventory entries flagged worn/invested/equipped; it never looks at `inv.runes.property`. The only reads of `inv.runes.property` in the whole repo are derive.ts:994/1325/1532 and companions.ts:730, all of which take `db.runes[p]?.damage` — and runes.shadow has no `damage`. So items.shadow.passiveEffects {skills:{stealth:1}} is unreachable the moment the rune is etched, and the Stealth breakdown is short by 1. The one lane an etched rune DOES reach is FEAT_SITUATIONAL, because explain.ts:200 pushes every `inv.runes.property` id into characterSituationalIds — which is where the entry has to go.

records.reason: Two independent errors. (1) The cited precedent does not exist: of 107 spellhearts, 71 print a numeric resistance and ZERO carry passiveEffects.resistances (the '6' are non-spellhearts like emberheart and ochre-fulcrum-lens). (2) The field cannot fire. play.ts:746 attachItem sets `{attachedTo, worn:false, equipped:false, invested:false}`, and both resistance readers gate on `inv.worn || inv.invested || inv.equipped` (derive.ts:707) as does passiveItemBonus (derive.ts:220) — so an AFFIXED spellheart is invisible to passiveEffects, and the Armor benefit applies only while affixed. The proposed fix is inert exactly when the rule fires and would fire only in the one state where it must not (a loose statuette, or one affixed to a WEAPON, where the Weapon benefit applies instead). Same gate silently kills the already-shipped FEAT_SITUATIONAL AC entry at :2357. This needs the attachment gate widened the way property runes were (explain.ts:200 pushes `inv.runes.property` for precisely this reason), and then an effectChoices Armor/Weapon pick carrying the resistance in `grant.passive` — not a blanket passiveEffects.
records.quote: - **Armor** You gain resistance 1 against ranged weapon attacks.

records.reason: Identical to the base grade: no spellheart in core.json carries passiveEffects.resistances, and an affixed spellheart has worn/equipped/invested all false (play.ts:746), so derive.ts:707 never reads it. The resistance 5 would apply while the statuette sits loose in a pack and vanish the moment it is affixed to armour. Needs the attachment gate plus an Armor/Weapon effectChoices grant, not a blanket passiveEffects.
records.quote: - **Armor** You gain resistance 5 against ranged weapon attacks.

records.reason: The stated reason — 'SituationalTarget has no companion-strike kind — every kind names a stat of the character' — is contradicted by the sweep's own three companion verdicts in this same chunk. swift-eel-mount (a MOUNT's AC and saves), swift-support (a MOUNT's Speed) and undead-eidolon (an EIDOLON's saves) were all called MISS with character-stat kinds and mount-naming wording, on the shipped precedents soul-vessel-mount (situationalBonuses.ts:580) and battle-saddle (:1940). `kind:'strikeAttack'` is available on exactly the same terms, and swift-support is the closest analogue of all: also triggered by commanding the companion, also lasting until the start of your next turn.
